events.title: Bowl of ‘Zole Brooklyn
events.description:
Bowl of ‘Zole Brooklyn Returns: 30+ Chefs, Pozole and 300 Agave Pours.
Thirty-plus kitchens. More than 300 pours of agave and regional Mexican spirits. One steaming bowl of pozole after another. On Thursday, October 22, Bowl of ‘Zole returns to Brooklyn’s Industry City for a four-hour deep dive into classic Mexican cuisine and cultura líquida—and for anyone in the food, beverage, or hospitality business, it’s a rare chance to taste where Mexican dining in New York is heading next.
This isn’t a generic tasting event. The 2026 lineup stacks James Beard Foundation nominees, Michelin-recognized restaurants, and StarChefs Rising Stars winners alongside independent neighborhood kitchens from across the five boroughs. That mix—celebrated names and under-the-radar operators under one roof—is exactly what makes grassroots festivals like this a working scouting trip for operators, buyers, and beverage directors.

events.title: Exhibit – ECHO: An Introduction to the Inner Self
events.description:
Creative Vice and Lista Studios presents ECHO: An Introduction to the Inner Self, the first solo exhibition by Randy Richard Morales in New York City.
Echo began as a character created by the artist to separate the negative voice in his head from the truth. Over time, that character became an entire world—a way for him to explore self-doubt, identity, relationships, innocence, growth, and the emotions we carry with us.
After months of creating at LISTA Studio, he’s opening the doors and sharing Echo World with everyone.
Opening Reception October 23 · 5:30–8 PM LISTA Studio · New York Come see the work, meet Echo, have a drink, and celebrate.

He has opened for big acts like Mark Normand, Rachel Feinstein and Cipha Sounds. He just finished his stint as a radio personality on New York radio station 94.7 the block. When he’s not touring the country or seas, Liam performs all over New York City and uploads sketches to his social media daily. Hoodo Hersi is a Toronto-based comedian currently writing on A24/Amazon’s Untitled Ramy Youssef Animated show. Since being selected as a New Face: Canada at the Just For Laughs Festival in Montreal, and being selected as one of CBC’s 15 Comics to Watch, Hoodo has performed in clubs and festivals all over Canada and the United States, including the Winnipeg Comedy Festival and the BBC World Service Montreal Comedy Show where both of her performances aired on the CBC, She was also selected as an Audible New Voice at SF Sketchfest, and performed with Hasan Minhaj, Lil Rel Howery, Chris Redd, Gina Yashere, Roy Wood Jr., Nicole Byer, and Maria Bamford, among others. She also had the distinct honors of hosting the TEDxToronto Conference and featuring in Sephora’s national “Get Lippie” lipstick campaign in partnership with Fashion Magazine, where she was profiled as one of the three Female Comedians Taking Canada by Storm Right Now.Dave Temple is the Spotlight stealing comic that has clubs managers and college bookers across the country asking, "Where did you find this guy?!" Originally from Philadelphia, Dave began stand-up comedy as a challenge amongst friends. Dave brings an unadulterated view on life and his immediate surroundings with a poignancy that is unparalleled and leaves every single audience in stitches. Dave has appeared on TruTV's LaffMobb LaffTracks, Showtime at the Apollo, VH1 Live as well as his own YouTube Show #LOOKATITTHISWAYFunny, smart, fresh, and magnetic, Neko White is a star. A comedian born and raised in Harlem, Neko has brought his unique perspective and sharp comedy from New York to international audiences. Beginning his career at just fourteen years old, the then high school freshman was sitting in class when a teacher asked, “Does anyone have a talent?” Something in Neko’s mind said, “Go tell jokes!“ He went up in front of his classmates and it worked. And, as they say, the rest is history. As a stand-up, Neko has been featured on Netflix’s "Pete Davidson Presents: The Best Friends," Cracked Comedy Club, TruTV’s "Laff Tracks," AXS TV’s "Gotham Comedy Live," STARZ’s "New York’s Funniest," and Kevin Hart’s LOL Network. He was named one of the "New Faces" in the Just For Laughs Festival, performed in Netflix is a Joke Festival, and won Carolines’ prestigious March Madness competition. Neko released a comedy album titled "Marscellus," then produced one of the most original filmed specials in recent memory with his self-released "Dark Out." Shot with no audience, a pitch-black background, and recorded with an old-fashioned microphone, Neko’s special received critical acclaim. One publication said "Dark Out" made Neko one of the “innovators changing comedy.” Neko also self-produced his first hour special, "Neko White: Introducing Me.” He was the subject of the award-winning documentary, “One Mic.”Neko is an accomplished television personality. He hosted Vice News’ popular series, "How To Be A Person" and has been a regular guest on MTV2’s "Hip Hop Hollywood Squares" and Comedy Central’s "Dark Humor." Neko made his film acting debut in the movie, "Midlife."

events.title: Barrel Age Your Own Sake — A Brooklyn Kura Workshop Class
events.description:
*What You’ll Create
A functional 2-liter oak barrel, coopered from scratch — same craft, same tools, same afternoon of assembling staves and hoops, cutting crozes on the router table, and charring the interior until it’s ready for spirits. This time, what goes in it isn’t whiskey. It’s rice, koji, yeast, and water, aged into something you helped choose.
*The Tasting Flight
A sake expert from Brooklyn Kura walks you through a flight of three sakes and a shochu, all brewed or distilled right here in Industry City, all selected because they take well to a little time in wood. The lineup changes with the seasons, but here’s what’s been on the table:
Grand Prairie — a Junmai Ginjo built around white peach, jasmine, and toasted rice.
Occidental — a dry-hopped Junmai, bringing out lychee, grapefruit, and cherry that age into deeper dried-fruit notes. Tidal — a fuller-bodied
Junmai, all steamed rice, apple, and cereal bran.
Kura Shochu — distilled from the leftover sake lees, rich with fig and custard and a rice umami built for barrel aging.
Finishing the Night at Kura
Your barrel’s made, your glass is empty — Brooklyn Kura is a short walk across Industry City, and your Craftsman Ave ticket gets you a discount on sake or shochu to take home and age. They’ve got a full kitchen too: mac and cheese, little smoky sausages, house-made focaccia. Good reason to stay a while longer.
